title: Magnetically-Assisted Remote Controlled Microcatheter Tip Deflection under Magnetic Resonance Imaging
protocol: Obtain a commercially available microcatheter for a substrate.
Ensure catheters have no ferrous components and are MR-safe.
Sputter a titanium adhesion layer onto an insulating tube.
Deposit a copper seed layer onto the titanium layer.
Electrodeposit a positive photoresist layer using Shipley's PEPR-2400.
Expose the photoresist using a laser direct-write system in the pattern of the desired coil form.
Develop the exposed photoresist in a 1% solution of potassium carbonate at 35 °C.
Electroplate copper through the remaining resist mask to form the desired coil.
Remove the resist with hot developer after copper electrodeposition.
Remove the copper seed layer from the insulating tube.
Remove the titanium adhesion layer.
Attach the insulating tube to the catheter tip using shrink wrap.
Cover the entire coiled tip with shrink wrap.
Place insulating tube structures inside each other for multi-axis catheters.
Thread copper wires through the lumen of the microcatheter and solder to the coils at the tip.
Modify a 6 ft RJ11 phone cable to 3 ft in length.
Connect the copper wires emanating from the back end hub of the microcatheter to the modified 3 ft phone jack transmission line.
Make a small hole in the center of the side of a plastic basin about 5 cm from the bottom.
Insert a 9F Avanti Cordis vascular sheath through the hole.
Cut the distal tip of the vascular sheath, leaving a 4 cm-long piece extending into the basin.
Attach a rotating hemostatic or Thuoy-Borst valve to the end of the sheath for stabilization.
Fill the basin with distilled water to ensure complete submersion of the apparatus.
Insert the catheter with coiled tip through the vascular sheath and valve.
Measure and record the unrestrained length of the microcatheter extending from the valve into the waterbath.
Place the waterbath with microcatheter system within the magnet of the MR scanner.
Orient the waterbath with respect to the bore of the magnet.
Connect the modified 3 ft phone cable to a 25 ft RJ11 phone cable using a 2-way phone jack.
Place one end of the 25 ft phone cable to a Lambda LPD-422A-FM dual regulated power supply.
Position the transmission lines through a waveguide and place outside of the MR scanner room beyond the 5 Gauss line.
Construct a hollow vessel phantom with a Y-shaped intersection from rubber tubing before experimentation.
Fill the vessel phantom with a 0.0102 M gadopentetate dimeglumine solution in distilled water.
Assemble the microcatheter system as outlined in steps 1.1 through 1.9.
Connect the catheter to the power supply and position it according to steps 2.9 to 2.11.
Place the tip of the microcatheter at the base of the vessel opening.
Position the phantom within the magnet bore of the MR scanner.
Perform imaging with a 1.5T clinical MR system (Siemens Avanto, SW: Syngo B13 or Philips Achieva, SW release 2.1).
Apply 50 mA of current to visualize the catheter tip position.
Observe tip deflection in the water bath setup when applying variable amounts of current from ±100 mA.
Record consecutive applications of set amounts of current.
Push the catheter by hand to advance it through the vessel phantom while applying current at the branch point.
Deflect the catheter tip into the desired vessel using applied current.
Advance the catheter into the branch vessel by manually pushing the catheter end.
Retract the catheter to the vessel bifurcation and repeat in the opposite branch.
Acquire MR images using a 2D snapshot-FLASH sequence with specified parameters.
